findings.passage: The second front opened in June, when an export-control directive forced Anthropic to switch off its newest models for all customers.
findings.problem: The record was accuracy-checked on 2026-10-05, yet the body, the G7 FAQ (C103) and C53 all stop at the June 12 switch-off. Anthropic's own post of June 30, 2026, 'Redeploying Claude Fable 5' (https://www.anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5, opened for this review), says: 'As of today, June 30, the export controls on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 have been lifted,' and that Fable 5 'will be available starting tomorrow, Wednesday, July 1, to users globally.' The Pentagon front in the same section ends on its dated court outcome; this one has no ending, and the FAQ implies a shutdown that never ended. C53 and C103 are marked stable with no trigger, so nothing in the record would prompt the fix later.
findings.acceptance_test: The section and the G7 FAQ answer each add one dated clause saying the controls were lifted on June 30, 2026 and Fable 5 returned globally on July 1. The clause is sourced to Anthropic's June 30, 2026 post, added to the evidence record as an opened source and cited by C53 and C103. No detail beyond what the opened source states is added. A reader in 2031 can tell how, and how fast, the second front ended.

The decisive one, 'I have 3,000 people who are on the same page as me' and 'I never feel like I'm alone' (C179), comes from a local whisper transcript of S59 that research_tasks marks 'REQUIRED before publication: a human must re-listen.' findings.problem: 'For a decade' is measured from the writing date, so it drifts: a 2031 reader will take it as 2021-2031. It's also imprecise now. The pattern the article documents starts at Baidu in the mid-2010s and runs through the OpenAI exit sequence (2017-2020) to Anthropic (2021-2026). This is the thesis sentence (C192), so the drift matters most here.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence is anchored to where the pattern starts, not to the present (for example 'Since his Baidu years in the mid-2010s' or 'From Baidu to Anthropic'). No duration in the body is measured from the writing date.

findings.passage: Until this October 2026 revision, this page typed him as a Five.
findings.problem: 'This October 2026 revision' is deictic. After the next refresh it will name the wrong revision. The retype is also narrated twice: here and again at 'The Five reading, which this page held until October 2026'. The draft says 'this page' nine times. The similarity scanner's 0.041 trip against Rebecca-Yarros rests only on that shared phrase ('thi page'). The arguments differ, so this is not cross-profile reuse, but the tic is real inside this draft, and page-history narration is the part of the text a five-year reader needs least.
findings.acceptance_test: The retype is disclosed once, with an absolute date and no 'this revision' deixis (for example 'Until October 2026, 9takes typed him as a Five'). 'This page' appears no more than about three times, kept where it marks inference (for example 'this page infers none').

findings.passage: He also calls himself "one of the most bullish about AI capabilities improving very fast," a confidence that is a real cost to the Six reading, whose hallmark is doubt.
findings.problem: Several time-bound claims are undated, or dated only relative to other events. (1) This forecasting stance is written in the present tense with no date. It comes from July 30, 2025 (S02), events will test or revise his capability forecasts within five years, and C41 is stable with no trigger. (2) 'The courts have since ruled one of the Pentagon's two designations unlawful and upheld the other' names no dates or courts in the prose. S22 and S23 give August 27, 2026 (a federal judge in San Francisco) and September 25, 2026 (a 2-1 D.C. appeals panel). (3) 'confidentially filed for an IPO ... in June' has no year. (4) 'the phrase he would use for his whole company the next year' leaves the reader to work out June 2026.
findings.acceptance_test: Each of the four passages carries an absolute date in the prose: July 2025; August 27, 2026 and September 25, 2026, with the court named; June 2026; June 2026. C41 becomes time_sensitive, with a trigger to re-weigh the 'real cost to the Six reading' sentence when his public capability forecasts come due or he revises them.

assessment: Five-year test: the thesis passes. The type argument rests on interpersonal evidence from the mid-2010s to 2026: Baidu, the OpenAI exit sequence, the 2022 'trust and common purpose' line, the 2024 Lex answer and Daniela's 2026 account. Removing the September 2026 essay, the evaluator pledge, the pacing turn and the October 2026 Quartz report leaves that argument intact. The November 2025 hook is durable. Hook paragraphs two and three and the closing section are the perishable layer, and most of it is dated and tracked (C43, C42, C164, C56, C30, C52, C67, C187). Gaps: the closing open question has no trigger, and C30 would delete its best test (future-01). The June 2026 export-control episode ended on June 30, 2026, according to Anthropic's own post, but the body, the FAQ and the record omit the ending (future-02). The type section's discriminator leads with a June 2026 quote still awaiting the required audio check, which this review could not do because caption retrieval was IP-blocked (future-03). Relative durations, deictic page history and undated stances need absolute anchors (future-04 to future-06), and two triggers need repair (future-07). The similarity scanner tripped at 0.041 against Rebecca-Yarros on the phrase 'this page' alone. The arguments differ, so this is not formulaic reuse. Standard profile, not an open case. Risk flags are carried unchanged.
